response.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_product_quantity) as avg_avg_product_quantity, AVG(num_order_items) as avg_num_order_items, AVG(share_of_all_items) as avg_share_of_all_items FROM (SELECT pc.product_type_description, AVG(per_product.avg_quantity) as avg_product_quantity, AVG(per_product.order_item_count) as num_order_items, AVG(per_product.share) as share_of_all_items FROM (SELECT p.product_id, p.production_type_code, AVG(CAST(oi.product_quantity AS DECIMAL)) as avg_quantity, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) as order_item_count, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Order_Items) as share FROM Products p INNER JOIN Order_Items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.production_type_code) per_product JOIN Product_Categories pc ON per_product.production_type_code = pc.production_type_code GROUP BY pc.product_type_description) per_type

assumptions.assumption: Uses INNER JOIN to exclude products with no order items. 'Ignore missing values' is interpreted as excluding products where average quantity cannot be computed (those with zero orders).
product_quantity (stored as VARCHAR(50)) is cast to DECIMAL for numeric averaging.

alternatives.interpretation: Use LEFT JOIN to include all products, with NULL average quantities ignored by AVG(), but zero order counts and zero shares included in the per-type averaging. This would skew per-type averages toward products with no orders.
